newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down awaiting property bonds.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down awaiting property bonds.

text.p: Thai stocks eased slightly in moderate trade on Thursday as investors sold large capitalised stocks while awaiting the launch of government's zero-coupon bonds to help the depressed property sector, brokers said.

Some investors were cautious about how much the zero-coupon bonds would aid the property sector. " They still don't have full confidence on this initiative," said Busaba Kunasirin of Chao Phya Finance and Securities.
The SET composite index fell 3.59 points to 716.68 on 4.4 billion baht turnover.
Brokers said the lack of fresh, positive news compounded by investor caution about the zero-coupon bonds also sparked some profit-taking after recent rises.
Several major sectors fell on Thursday.

The banking sector fell most in value terms by 0.31 percent and trading in the sector amounted to about 20 percent of total turnover. The finance sector gained 0.38 percent while trading in the sector was 14.14 percent of the total turnover.
Brokers said Thursday's retraction in the index was good for the market after gains were posted over the past four days.
Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, falling 0.75 baht to 38. Media operator Wattachak rose 1.50 to 16.50 after denying earlier in the day that it was facing financial problems.
Advanced Info Services was unchanged at 236 and Electricity Generating slipped 1.50 to 60.50.
Support on Friday was seen by some brokers at around 700-point and resistance at 730.
